title: GoOrganicAfrica 44-country calculator data readiness matrix
scope: Tracks evidence-to-calculator completion for the 44 countries outside the 10 existing active profiles. This is a work queue, not a certification of data quality or a source of values for calculations.
safeguards: Do not modify the 10 active country profiles or calculator formulas in this workstream.
Do not activate a country until all required commodity-level values have provenance, dates, units, regional scope and validation.
Never fill missing prices, yields or costs with invented values.
Keep national statistics, market prices, farmgate prices and modelled estimates clearly distinguished.

batch_01_review.source_notes: Benin ESA 2024 dataset was released 11 June 2026; survey includes crop area, production, yields and input-use indicators, but not yet a complete set of enterprise cost budgets. DSA reports 2023/24 output indicators for maize, rice, cassava and soybean. Official 2025 cereal output estimate is about 2.9 million tonnes; aggregate only, not a crop-specific calculator yield.
blockers: Download and extract ESA 2024 crop-by-crop tables with area, output, yield, region and season.
Obtain dated farmgate prices by crop and department.
Obtain actual seed, fertilizer, crop protection, labour and machinery prices; ESA input-use indicators alone do not establish current unit costs.
Build and validate crop enterprise budgets.

batch_03_review.source_notes: A second official route was confirmed through INStaD's agricultural statistics page. It publishes a definitive 2023/24 campaign report PDF (listed 912.77 KB), 2023 macro-agricultural indicators, and the 2022 National Agricultural Census volumes, including a 37.49 MB principal tables volume and a 22.96 MB main results volume. INStaD states that annual crop area and production series are sourced from the Ministry's Directorate of Programming and Forecasting and that yield is production divided by area. The linked 2023/24 PDF endpoint returned HTTP 503 during retrieval, so no crop-level values were transcribed in this batch. FAO's ESA 2024 interactive tables remain linked but returned HTTP 403.
blockers: Retry or obtain the INStaD definitive 2023/24 campaign PDF through an alternate official download route.
Extract crop-by-crop planted/harvested area, production and regional tables from the campaign report and census volumes.
Reconcile campaign statistics with ESA 2024 survey estimates; do not combine different reference periods without documenting definitions.
Obtain dated farmgate prices and input costs separately; the ESA 2024 core release does not include the full ILP/Machinery cost modules.

batch_04_review.source_notes: Successfully retrieved searchable text from the official DSA definitive 2023-2024 campaign report. Extracted national production and selected yield observations for maize, rice, sorghum, millet, yam, cassava, cowpea/beans, groundnut, soybean, tomato, chilli pepper, okra and onion. Report states the crop statistics came from DSA's Agricultural Statistical Survey across 10,245 holdings and 683 agricultural enumeration zones. These are national historical values, not region-level budgets. The report's summary table conflicts with its narrative and detailed Table 5 on soybean output (421,886 vs 520,929 tonnes); the soybean figure is withheld pending reconciliation.
blockers: Extract regional ESA 2024 / RNA tables and reconcile the national report.
Validate chart readings and any internal source table inconsistencies before use.
Obtain dated regional farmgate prices, input costs, labour, irrigation and machinery costs.
Construct regional budgets and calculator tests.
Resolve the conflicting soybean production values in the official report before numeric use.
batch_04_review.regional_lookup: 12 official departments added to src/_data/calculator/regions.json on the readiness branch; lookup only, not activated.

batch_01_review.source_notes: FAO reported official 2024 aggregate cereal production of 6.1 million tonnes, about 20% above the previous five-year average; localized production deficits and access constraints were noted in conflict-affected regions. FAO/50x2030 announced release of the 2024/25 Permanent Agricultural Survey and RGA phase-II horticulture/arboriculture modules on 15 October 2026. FAO GIEWS recorded May 2025 millet and sorghum wholesale price movements, which are historical wholesale observations, not current farmgate prices.

batch_05_review.source_notes: Official Ministry and Presidency sources confirm July 2025 reorganisation from 13 to 17 regions and from 45 to 47 provinces. batch_13_review.source_notes: The prefecture selector contains 20 entries: 18 administrative prefectures, two economic prefectures and Bangui as the capital prefecture/commune in the commonly used 20-unit list. Do not confuse this with ICASEES's seven broad statistical/administrative regions published in its 2025 provisional census tables. Before joining historical crop records, confirm the current official prefecture coding and boundaries.
agricultural_evidence: FAO GIEWS reference date 15 July 2026: 2026 maize planting was completed in central/southern areas under near-average planted area; harvest expected from mid-August. Northern millet/sorghum planting completed in early July; harvest expected from October. Conflict and displacement continue to restrict access to fields and inputs.

FEWS NET September 2026 update: August maize market prices were reported at 514 FCFA/kg in Birao and 257 FCFA/kg in Bangui. These are market prices, not farmgate quotations, and should not be inserted as farmgate values.

Secondary FAOSTAT/World Bank-derived series reports 2024 cereal production of 282,868 tonnes and yield of 788 kg/ha. This is a national cereal aggregate and must not be treated as crop-specific or prefecture-specific evidence.
batch_13_review.regional_lookup: 20 prefecture-level entries added to src/_data/calculator/regions.json as lookup only. Two economic prefectures are included in the 20-unit list; Bangui is a special capital unit. Validate the official administrative code crosswalk before data joins.
blockers: Obtain primary ICASEES/Ministry crop tables by prefecture, crop, season, area and production; derive yield only when area and production share matching definitions and years.
Reconcile the 20 prefecture list with ICASEES's seven broad regions and current boundary/coding instruments.
Obtain dated farmgate prices by commodity, grade, market and unit. Keep FEWS NET market prices labelled as market observations, not farmgate.
Obtain current seed, fertilizer, crop protection, irrigation/energy, labour and machinery costs.

safeguards: No active calculator profile or formula changed.

batch_12_review.administrative_geography: 23 province-level entries added as a regional selector only. The dataset lists 23 provinces and distinguishes 70 departments and 348 sub-prefectures; do not mix lower administrative levels into the province selector.
source_notes: The Presidency of Chad describes the country as having 23 administrative regions/provinces. A current administrative-divisions dataset lists 23 provinces, 70 departments and 348 sub-prefectures. Older and alternative spellings/names require a formal crosswalk before linking historical crop observations.
FEWS NET identifies the INSEED-linked Chad Data Portal as the operational source for crop statistics archive covering 2010–2023; detailed crop/province values still need extraction.

FAO GIEWS (reference date 7 September 2026) estimates 2025 aggregate cereal production at about 3 million tonnes, around 10% above the previous five-year average. It reports uncertain 2026 crop prospects following irregular rainfall, dry spells and poor vegetation in several provinces.

SESRIC reports 2024 national cereal harvested area of 3,276,392 ha, production of 2,709,156 tonnes and yield of 826.90 kg/ha. This is an aggregate cross-source indicator, not a crop-by-province yield table and not a farmgate price.
batch_12_review.regional_lookup: 23 province names added to src/_data/calculator/regions.json as lookup only; Chad remains not_active.

batch_06_review.source_notes: Added 31 administrative regions to the research-branch regional lookup. batch_15_review.source_notes: Verified the nine first-level provinces using the Gabon Ministry of Interior territorial-organisation page, which separately reports 48 departments, 52 communes, 26 districts and 164 cantons. The Ministry of Agriculture's RGA report page confirms the national agricultural census and lists its report volumes. FAO GIEWS' 4 June 2026 brief reports cassava and plantain as the main food crops, small maize production, a 2026 cereal import requirement forecast of 255,000 tonnes and above-average first-half rainfall that may have affected the secondary maize crop. Existing research evidence includes RGA/EPVA survey leads and World Bank sector context, but the crop/province tables and current enterprise costs remain unextracted.

batch_01_review.source_notes: Senegal released EAA 2024/25 data in June 2026. The annual survey covers all 14 regions and 45 departments. The 2024/25 Income, Labour and Productivity module captures input use and associated costs, alongside horticulture, livestock and fisheries/aquaculture. This is a strong source for building budgets, but the crop-level tables and microdata still need extraction and review.
blockers: Download DAPSA data portal tables and ANADS microdata catalogue records.

Build regionally representative enterprise budgets.

batch_02_review.source_notes: The FAO-hosted DAPSA catalogue exposes a public variable dictionary for the 2024-2025 EAA. PARCELLE_P1_ano contains 15,809 cases and 285 variables, including household/parcel IDs, survey weights, region, agroecological zone, declared parcel area in hectares and principal crop. prodpluv_ano contains 10,580 cases and 147 variables, including region, agroecological zone, crop, harvested quantity, sale quantity, sale unit, and average unit sale price. base_intrant_ano contains 5,191 cases and 15 variables, including input type, region, agroecological zone, quantity, unit, amount paid and unit price paid. maindeouevrembauche_ano contains 1,309 cases and 12 variables, including region, agroecological zone, worker category, number hired, days, hours per day, payment method and amount paid per person. These dictionaries prove that the survey has relevant fields; they do not provide extracted national means or verified crop budgets.
extraction_findings: Crop-area/yield work must join parcel area and principal-crop records with crop production records, preserving household/parcel keys, survey weights, region and agroecological-zone definitions.
Household-reported crop sales unit prices are available as survey variables but require unit conversion and plausibility checks before being labelled farmgate prices.
Input costs can be derived from the survey's amount-paid and quantity/unit fields only after product type, unit comparability, survey weights and outlier checks are resolved.
Paid labour cost fields exist, but operation-level labour and family labour valuation require separate treatment.
Public catalogue metadata and dictionaries are accessible; microdata download appears to require the catalogue's Get Microdata workflow/login and has not yet been obtained in this review.
blockers: Obtain authorised microdata access or public aggregated tables; do not redistribute confidential microdata.
Extract and join crop, parcel, input and labour tables using documented keys and survey weights.
Verify local units and conversion tables before computing yields or unit costs.
Obtain machinery, irrigation/energy and current market-level price evidence where survey coverage is insufficient.
Build regional enterprise budgets and calculator tests only after data extraction and validation.

batch_03_access_update.source_notes: The official Senegal ANADS catalogue provides a distinct national catalogue record for EAA 2024-2025 (SEN-DAPSA-EAA2024-2025-v1), with related materials including Phase 1 and Phase 2 questionnaires, an enumerator manual and local-to-standard crop measurement conversion workbooks. The catalogue metadata says the survey covers all 45 departments, but the anonymised microdata replaces department with agroecological zone while retaining region. It also explicitly requires confidentiality and restricts microdata use to aggregated statistical outputs; the microdata cannot be copied or passed to other organisations without DAPSA written authorisation. This is a legal/data-governance access condition, not merely a technical download issue.
blockers: Request and comply with DAPSA access conditions before using restricted microdata.
Prefer official aggregate tables if available for public use.
Use the official local-unit conversion workbooks before calculating crop yields or comparing household sale prices.
Do not treat anonymised agroecological-zone results as department-level results.

batch_04_review.source_notes: FAO's official Senegal access-to-data page links the EAA 2024-2025 interactive statistical tables. The FAO-linked DAPSA Open Data for Africa gallery resolves to https://senegal.opendataforafrica.org/gallery?tag=DAPSA but returned HTTP 403 in this retrieval attempt; table values were not extracted.
blockers: Resolve the public DAPSA portal's HTTP 403 or obtain aggregate tables through an alternate official route.
Extract public regional tables and apply official local-unit conversion workbooks.
Obtain dated regional farmgate prices and input/labour costs.
Use aggregate outputs only; respect DAPSA microdata confidentiality and authorisation rules.
Build regional enterprise budgets and calculator tests.
